chapters.title: Chapter 5830: Purpose!
paragraphs: A part of Noah slipped quietly out of his Domain and into the Dream Engine.

He had no particular reason for it. Poona was busy bouncing around his hills, trying to taste the river of light. The cocoons on the hill were still closed. And the rest of him was already turning toward the Basal Floor and the rift. But somewhere between all of that, a thought had surfaced, and he had followed it.
He wanted to talk to someone!
Out of every dreamer sleeping on the golden shore, one name had come to mind.
He stepped into Bob’s dream.
It was full of Wheels!
Dead ones. Countless dead Wheels of Existence, hanging in a grey sky that went on forever. Every one of them was broken. Spokes snapped. Rims crakced through. Hubs crumbled to calcified dust.
And every one of them was trying to rebuild itself!

A spoke would drift back toward its hub and fit itself into place. A shard of rim would find another shard and fuse. For a moment, a Wheel would look almost whole, turning slowly, light flickering across its rim where life might once have been. Then a crack would race across it, and it would come apart again, and the pieces would drift, and begin again.
Over and over. Thousands of them, as far as the eye could see. Building, breaking, building.
Noah stood among them for a while and watched.

He knew this dream. Once, he had stood on the Calcified Wheels of the Null Cradle once, beside Thauron’s shadow, and looked down at a tentacled thing that had lost everything. He knew which Wheel had broken first for Bob.
At the center of the dream, a cocoon of hazy blue-gold light hung among the drifting spokes, glowing softly. Bob’s. Like every other Kin in the Dream Engine, still closed, still changing slowly.
Noah reached out and touched it.
He poured a little of himself into it. Just a little, enough to say: hurry up.
|Kin recognized: Bob.|
|Kin Evolution accelerated by your will.|
The cocoon brightened, then shuddered, then split down its middle like a seed pod in summer!
A figure stepped out!

It was humanoid, mostly. A round bald head, silver shading into gold, smooth and gleaming like a polished pebble. A body that stood upright, broad-shouldered and easy. But where arms and legs should have been, there were tentacles, long and supple and silver-gold, curling and uncurling lazily as they found their balance. And in the round face, two eyes like singularities, dark and deep and faintly glowing, looking out at the dream with mild surprise.
Something burned in his chest. Obsidian and violet, slow and wild, the colors of a storm given shape.
|Kin Evolution: Bob has emerged first among your Kin.|
|Root formed: THE Khaotic Chorionic Gonadotropin. Root of Khaos.|
|Saturation toward Immensity: 9%. The road to his Immensity is long.|
Bob flexed a tentacle. Then another. He looked down at himself, at the violet storm turning in his chest, and then up, at the man standing among his broken Wheels.
His singularity eyes squinted.
"Now this is rare," Bob said."A visit from the big guy himself?"
He tilted his round head. "What brought you to my dream?"
Noah shrugged.
"I just felt like talking to someone," he said. "And for some reason, you came to mind, Little Bobby."
Bob stared at him for a moment.
Then he laughed and shook his gleaming head!
Clouds began to form around them!

They came out of Noah without him asking, soft and golden, drifting up between the broken Wheels and gathering in loose piles, as clouds gather on a lazy afternoon. Noah lowered himself onto one and sat back against it, stretching out his legs, and looked up.

Above them, the grey sky of Bob’s dream began to change. Noah’s dreams leaked into it as warmth leaks into a cold room. Stars came out between the dead Wheels, blue and gold. A faint shape of a great Tree glimmered for a moment far overhead, its trunk climbing out of sight, and faded. A golden-blue panda drifted past on a cloud, yawning, and disolved into mist.
Bob watched the panda go by with one eyebrow raised, or the place an eyebrow would be.
"Your dreams are...as grand as ever," he said.
"Mmm."

Bob coiled himself onto a golden cloud of his own, tentacles tucked under him, and settled in. For a while, both of them stayed quiet. They simply sat there among the Wheels and the clouds, two old enemies on a quiet afternoon.
It had been weeks, Noah thought.

Or it had been Ages. Telling the difference had grown hard. Time felt different to him now. It ran in periods rather than in a line. It sat around him in periods, like rooms in a house he could walk between: the room where he had first met this creature, the room where they had fought, the room on the Middle Wheel Platform, the room where he had reached into a broken father’s life and pulled his daughter out of it. All of them were still there. All of them had led here.
Noah let the clouds drift.
When Bob spoke again, his voice had changed.
"I...did everything I did for my daughter," he said. "It was not an excuse for all the ones who died while I sought to save her. I know that. I carry that."
His singularity eyes stayed on the broken Wheels, building and breaking, building and breaking. "But this is what we do. Fathers do everything they can for their children."
He turned his round head toward Noah.
"You have two now," Bob said. "And your Son is even messing around with my Daughter..."
A slow smile spread across his face.
"Hah. Is that why you came to me? Do you now consider me your in-law?"
He laughed, delighted with himself.
"Haha. We have come far..."
Noah tipped his head back against the cloud and smiled at the stars.
They had. They truly had!

He remembered the old Bob. A tentacled monster following the being who had crushed his own Wheel because that was the only road left that led toward his child. He remembered looking at that monster and thinking: pitiful. Noble, tragically so, and pitiful. A man held up by a single thread of regret.

And he remembered the day he had finally reached into that thread and pulled the daughter free, and eventually brought them both home into THE Infiniverse, and set them down among his own people. He remembered Hell Terra Firma, and the Prime Flame and Wheels of Existence...he remembered too many things!
"Everything here is yours." Bob waved a tentacle at the dream around them, the Wheels, the clouds, the stars.
"I live in your Infiniverse. I sleep in your Dream Engine. My daughter eats at your table and makes eyes at your son..."
They sat for a while longer.

A dead Wheel nearby came together almost completely, turning slowly, light flickering across its rim. Both of them watched it. It held for a long moment, longer than the others. Then a crack spread through it, and it drifted apart.
Bob sighed.
"You know," he said, "no matter how high you climb, it all comes back to the same few things."
Noah looked over at him.
"Power," Little Bobby went on, slowly, as a man talks when he has been thinking about something for a very long time.

"Complexity. True Sources. Lattices. Wheels. Now Roots and Immensity and whatever else you have going on. I’ve seen beings rise so high they forgot what the ground looked like. I’ve seen Wheels that held more life than anyone could count, and I’ve watched them break."
His tentacles curled under him. "And at the bottom of all of it, under every power anyone has ever had, there’s the same thing."
He held up one tentacle and counted on it, tip by tip.
"To love. To protect. To provide."
The violet storm in his chest turned slowly.

"That’s it. That’s all of it. Whether it’s my daughter." He pointed the tentacle at Noah. "Or your son and daughter. We do everything we can for them. And for ourselves, so that we’re still standing when they need us. Everything else is just..." He waved at the broken Wheels. "Scenery."
Noah closed his eyes.
He nodded, slowly, and for a long while he stayed quiet.
"Sometimes I feel very distant from all of them," Noah said.
Bob turned his head.

"I see so much now," Noah went on. "Every path. Every branch. When I look at Seo-yeon, I can see a thousand versions of her growing up, all at once, all of them real. When I look at Henry, I see every choice he could make before he makes it. When I look at my mother, I see thr countless years she has left, and every way those years could go."
He was quiet for a moment. "It would be easy to stand up here and watch it all happen. To see everyone I love as patterns. Beautiful patterns, and very far away."
The clouds drifted around them.

"But the Human in me will not let me," he said. "My evolution took it and made it infinite. Every feeling I have now, it grows. It does not fade. I worry about them, and the worry keeps going. I love them, and it keeps going. I am angry for them, and it keeps going."

He opened his gold eyes and looked up at the stars his own dreams had put into Bob’s sky. "I used to wonder whether I would stop caring, someday. Whether a being like me eventually becomes too large to feel small things."
He smiled faintly. "I do not think I will. I think I will feel all of it, for as long as there is a me to feel it. I think I am going to keep caring for a very, very long time."
Bob only listened.
"Right now," Noah said, "almost everyone I love is in a cocoon."
He could see them, through the threads, even from here. A hill in his Domain with two shining shapes on it. The golden shore of THE Infiniverse lined with sleepers wrapped in light.
"Ruination. She has been with me since before I was anything. I hope she comes out of it knowing she was never just a voice in my head." He paused.
"THE Infiniverse. She has carried everything I own and everyone I love on her back without once complaining. I hope she comes out of it lighter. I hope she finds out what she wants for herself."

"My mother. I hope she comes out of it with nothing left to fear." His voice softened. "Seo-yeon. I hope she comes out of it curious, and stays curious, and never once has to be brave as I had to be. Henry. I hope he comes out of it strong enough to protect what he loves."
A glance toward Bob. "Including your daughter..."
Bob snorted.

"Emotive," Noah said. "I hope she comes out of it with every color she has, and none of them hurting. Thalia. I hope she comes out of it and rewrites whatever she likes. Barbatos. I hope her dead stand up for her forever. Ling, Poona..." He shook his head slowly. "All of them. I hope they come out bigger than they were, and still themselves."
He let out a long breath.
"I have been chasing power for a long time, Bob. I am still chasing it. I will chase it all the way down into where Those Who Remain have not even accessed, and eat everything I find."

He settled deeper into the cloud. "But you are right. Underneath all of it, that is the reason. I want to stand high enough that nothing can ever reach down and take them from me. And then I want to sit at the table with them, and eat, and argue, and smile."
Bob laughed softly.
"That," Noah said,"is the dream."
Above them, a dead Wheel drifted together.
Spoke by spoke, shard by shard, it came whole and began to turn, and this time, with a faint hum, Noah’s dream reached up into it, golden and patient, and held its cracks closed.
It stayed whole!
Bob watched it turn for a long moment, his singularity eyes very bright!

chapters.title: Chapter 5831: No Door Was Sealed! I
paragraphs: <THE Sealed One>
All of existence was red, and THE Sealed One stood at the center of it, smiling.

He had always liked this part. The moment before. When the crimson first poured out of him and painted everything it touched, every enemy in reach became, for one breath, a thing that belonged to his color. The obsidian foam of a dead home, the drifting snow, the rivers of ink around the woman on the air. All of it red. All of it, in a small and honest way, already his.
He let them look at it!
Across the undefinition, three figures stood in his light.
THE Creature, vast and dark, white and obsidian flames rising off him, the fractured Root of Existence glowing in the crack across his chest.

Anaximander beside him, a scholar in white robes with no authority at all, his hands clasped behind his back. And Calliope, THE Writer of Mythos, sitting on nothing with one leg crossed over the other, script crawling slowly across her skin.
Three of them. And behind him, five Immense Ones, standing in the foam like suns behind a hill, watching.
He had no need of them.
That was the point.
Calliope moved first!
She uncrossed her legs, lifted one ink-stained hand, and wrote on the air.
The words burned as she made them. Fine, dense lines of script, her own neat hand, unspooling from her fingertip in long black ribbons.
A dreamer would have recognized the shape of what she was doing; he had a Grammar of his own. But hers made stories, where his made Sentences.
"Once," Calliope said lazily, writing as she spoke, "there was a mountain that was told to kneel. And it refused. And the hand that told it to kneel broke on its peak."
The words left the air and became true!
A mountain rose out of the red foam between them, grey and vast and snowcapped, ancient as a myth, and it came down on THE Sealed One like a falling sky!
He lifted one hand, and caught it.

The crimson in his palm opened. It was Infinity, and something older under it, braided together into a single bright substance, and it drank. The mountain met his palm and began to come apart, stone by stone, myth by myth, each piece sliding into the red light of his hand and vanishing. He was eating it, eating her story.
Then he chewed, thoughtfully.
"Good," he said. "A little dry."
Calliope’s dark eyes narrowed, and the script on her skin quickened.
She wrote faster!

A tide came next, a flood from some story about the drowning of the first Dimension, roaring across the foam in a wall of black water full of drowned bells. A spear followed it, written out of a legend about a hunter who threw his weapon at the sun and pinned it to the sky. Then a crowd of shining soldiers out of a war that existed only in her hand, marching in perfect order, every one of them a myth of a hero who did not fall.
THE Sealed One met all of them.

He drank the flood. The spear he caught between two fingers, tasted, and let crumble. The soldiers reached him in their thousands, and he walked through them as through a field of tall grass, his crimson eating each one as it touched him, and with every myth he devoured, he shone a little brighter.
And THE Creature moved!

Instead of attacking, he did something worse. The foam around THE Sealed One stopped being foam. The red light, the drifting snow, the air between them, the very ground beneath the Sealed One’s feet: all of it became THE Creature. His Pantheon of All Existence had no shape. It became the surroundings, and now THE Sealed One stood inside him.
The space closed in!
Existence itself pressed down on THE Sealed One from every side, weight upon weight, the burden of eras pressing inward, and his feet sank. For a moment, the crimson around him flickered.
"Ah," THE Sealed One said softly. "This...is you Existence?"
He pushed outward.

Crimson tore through THE Creature’s Pantheon like light through cloth. The red brilliance poured out of him in every direction at once, Infinity and the old thing beneath it, and wherever it struck, THE Creature’s existence was eaten. Eaten, rather than broken. A chunk of his Pantheon simply ceased to be his and became a little more of THE Sealed One.
THE Creature grunted!
Then THE MAW opened!

It opened in the dark above THE Sealed One, vast and lightless, and it came down to swallow the crimson whole, one devourer meeting another. For an instant, the two appetites ground against each other, the MAW eating crimson, the crimson eating MAW, and the whole undefinition shook with the sound of it.
"Interesting," THE Sealed One murmured, and for the first time, he took a step back.
And a few strides away, Anaximander watched all of it with his hands clasped behind his back, and sweated.

His fight looked nothing like the others’. He had no authority to fight with. Every scrap of power in this place belonged to someone else: THE Creature’s existence, Calliope’s myths, the crimson of the man across from him.
All he had was himself.
THE Sealed One noticed him at last. He looked across the foam at the scholar in white, and something in his face brightened with real curiosity.
"You," he said. "I have seen many anomalies but...what exactly are you?"
WAA!
He flicked his fingers.
A lance of crimson tore across the undefinition toward Anaximander, Infinity and the source braided together, bright enough to unmake clusters of Dimensions.
Anaximander looked at it.
"No," he said. "That won’t reach me."
The lance stopped!

It hung in the air an arm’s length from his chest, crimson and blazing and perfectly still, straining forward with all the power of a fused Infinity behind it, and pressed no farther. Existence had heard the man in white robes speak, and existence agreed with him.
The lance faded.
THE Sealed One’s eyebrows rose.
He sent another. A storm of them this time, hundreds of crimson lances from every direction at once.
"You won’t hit her," Anaximander said, not even looking, and every lance curving toward Calliope bent away. "Or him."
The ones aimed at THE Creature broke apart!
"And you are not as fast as you think you are."
THE Sealed One, who had already crossed half the distance between them in the space of a thought, found himself somehow still standing where he had started.
He stopped!
For a long moment, he simply looked at Anaximander. At the sweat on the scholar’s brow. At the hollow in his chest shaped like a Root, filled with nothing but existence’s agreement.
Then THE Sealed One laughed!
It was a genuine laugh, bright and astonished.
"You," he said, "are the strongest one here."
He turned his whole attention onto the scholar, and his voice softened into something almost affectionate.

"The Creature commands existence. The Writer makes it. But you simply say what is true, and existence nods along. No authority. No Root of your own." He tilted his head. "Do you know how many things I have eaten, trying to understand how something like you happens? And here you are, sweating in the snow."
"It’s quite warm," Anaximander said mildly, "under all this red."
THE Sealed One stood still for a long time after that.

Behind him, the five Immense Ones watched without moving. Across from him, three enemies drew breath: THE Creature with a hole eaten in his Pantheon, Calliope with her script running thin across her skin, Anaximander with sweat on his brow and his hands still clasped behind him.
They had held him. All three together, they had held him.
He found that he was very pleased.

"Do you know what I am?" he asked them, quietly. "Most do not. They call me a thief. A genocidal maniac who ate his own disciples. A devourer. A vessel-wearer. They are not wrong. But they miss the point."
He spread his pale hands.

"Every being in existence is born with a little. A Root, if they are lucky. A Source. A gift from some framework they did not build. And they spend their whole lives guarding that little, and dying with it."

All of existence was red, and THE Sealed One stood at the center of it, smiling.
He had always liked this part.
The moment before.
When the crimson first poured out of him and painted everything it touched, every enemy in reach became, for one breath, a thing that belonged to his color.
The obsidian foam of a dead home, the drifting snow, the rivers of ink around the woman on the air.
All of it red.
All of it, in a small and honest way, already his.
He let them look at it!
Across the undefinition, three figures stood in his light.

Calliope moved first!
She uncrossed her legs, lifted one ink-stained hand, and wrote on the air.

Fine, dense lines of script, her own neat hand, unspooling from her fingertip in long black ribbons.

But hers made stories, where his made Sentences.

The words left the air and became true!

He lifted one hand, and caught it.
The crimson in his palm opened.

chapters.title: Chapter 5832: No Door Was Sealed! II
paragraphs: It was...stitched and grafted. Assembled out of a thousand pieces that had each been reaching for the door when he ate them. But Immensity, all the same, finished and heavy and real, pressing down on the undefinition from behind him.
The five Immense Ones at his back stirred, for the first time.
"My Chorus," THE Sealed One said fondly. "Every one of them died wanting to be Immense. So I let them be Immense together. Inside me."
He lifted his hand.
The Chorus moved with him.

It came down on THE Creature first. Crimson and a thousand braided colors, the full weight of stolen potential Immensity, crashing into the vast dark shape and driving it into the foam. White and obsidian flames guttered. The fractured Root in THE Creature’s chest flared, and cracked further, a new line of light splitting across it.

It came down on Calliope next. Her myths rose to meet it, mountains and floods and armies and suns, written faster than any hand should write, and the Chorus ate them all. Then it reached her. The script on her skin smeared and ran like ink in rain. She cried out once, sharp and furious, and fell from the air into the red foam.
And then it came for Anaximander.
"That won’t-" Anaximander began.
The Chorus spoke over him. A thousand stolen Roots, all at once, a single voice made of the voices of the dead:
|It will.|
And existence, for the first time, hesitated over whom to agree with.

That hesitation was enough. The weight came down. Anaximander was thrown across the undefinition, his white robes torn, blood at his mouth, and he lay where he fell, breathing hard, his eyes still open and still curious.
The crimson faded.
The Chorus settled behind THE Sealed One, quiet and enormous.
Three enemies lay broken in the foam of a dead home!
THE Sealed One stood over them, and smoothed down the front of his dark coat.
"I defeated you fairly," he said. "One against three. No help from behind me. You saw them. They did not move."
He glanced back at the five Immense Ones. "Fair and square."
He looked down at the three of them, and smiled.
"But will you play fair?"
He lifted his eyes.

Past the foam, past the red, past the edge of the undefinition, there was a place that only a very few beings could see. A vast and quiet brilliance, standing among shelves that climbed out of sight. Ink and parchment and patience.
THE MATRIARCH OF INK, watching over her fallen daughter.
THE Sealed One looked straight at her.
"I defeated your daughter," he said. "She is my spoil now. That is how these things go." His gold eyes glittered. "So. Will you be fair, Matriarch?"
He took a step toward Calliope.
"Or will you intervene?"
He took a second step!
And THE MATRIARCH OF INK’s power came down.

It spilled out of the hidden brilliance like a sea of ink pouring off a shelf, black and endless and furious, every drop of it a word, every word a law, falling on the undefinition from above. Its pressure crushed the foam flat. Its edges wrote themselves across the red sky in letters too vast to read.
|You will not touch my child.|
THE Sealed One laughed!
He threw back his head and laughed with real joy.
"There it is! Hypocrisy!"
Behind him, the five Immense Ones moved at last.
They rose out of the foam like five suns coming up at once, and their Immensity met the falling ink in the air above the undefinition, and the whole sky cracked.
"Remember!" THE Sealed One called up to them, still laughing. "You all played unfairly first!"
|Unfair is a word for the losing side,| one of the five answered, its voice like a bell rung underwater.
|Hold her,| said another, cold and flat. |Let the boy collect.|

The five of them pushed. The sea of ink pushed back. Above the undefinition, Immensity ground against Immensity in a storm of black and gold, and THE Matriarch’s brilliance strained against five at once, and slowly, slowly, was forced back toward her shelves.
And THE Sealed One walked toward his spoils.

He walked past THE Creature, groaning in the foam. Past Anaximander, propped on one elbow, watching him go with a calm that had blood on it. He walked to where Calliope lay with her script smeared and her eyes half open, and he crouched beside her, and reached out one pale hand.
Then the snow stopped falling!

Every flake hung in the air, perfectly still. The red light dimmed. The storm above them, five Immense Ones and one Matriarch locked together, slowed and grew quiet, as though the whole undefinition had stepped inside a house where someone was in mourning.
Frost spread across the foam!
It came in a slow, silver tide, ticking softly as it went, and where it passed, everything grew very cold and very calm. Out of it, walking without hurry, came a woman.

She was tall and pale, dressed in layers of grey like the light of a winter morning, her hair now bound up with silver pins. Her face held no anger. It held something older and heavier than anger, a grief kept so long and so carefully that it had become a kind of composure.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW!

Behind her, faint and flickering, stood a second figure. A man, translucent and illusory, sharp-faced and somber, with eyes far too bright for a ghost. He held a quill. Ancient, plain, its nib dark with something deeper than ink. It hummed in his illusory hand with a sound like a clock ticking very far away.
The Quill of Chronos!
THE Sealed One went still!
The Widow kept her gaze above him. She looked up, past the five Immense Ones, past the storm, toward the hidden shelves and the brilliance straining among them.
|Matriarch,| she said. Her voice was perfectly calm. |You will want to write with something.|
The illusory man behind her flicked his wrist.
The Quill of Chronos left his illusory fingers and flew upward, through the storm, past the five Immense Ones, straight into the hidden brilliance among the shelves.
THE MATRIARCH OF INK caught it!
For one long moment, the undefinition held its breath. Then, from the hidden place, came a sound that every being in the undefinition felt in their bones: an intake of breath. Shock. Disbelief.
|This is...|
Her power exploded upward!

The sea of ink became an ocean. It rose out of the hidden shelves in a single vast column and tore through the storm, and the five Immense Ones were flung back across the sky like leaves. The ink was words, and now it was time as well. Every letter now carried a tick of the Quill, every law a moment written and fixed, and where it fell, things that had happened began to be written differently.
The smears on Calliope’s skin began, slowly, to run backward.
THE Sealed One rose from his crouch, and looked at the Widow, and at the somber ghost behind her, and at the column of ink and time blazing up from the hidden shelves.
Then, quite deliberately, he sat down.
He sat on the frozen foam with one knee drawn up and his arm resting across it, in the middle of the undefinition, ringed by Immensity on every side.
Five Immense Ones regrouping above him. A Matriarch with a weapon of time in her hand. A Widow whose cold could still a storm. His Chorus of stolen Roots towering silent at his back.
And he looked entirely at ease.
"Everyone thinks the door is sealed," THE Sealed One said.
His voice was calm.

"The Long Night closed it. The First Frost swore it. The Counting presses on every Root in existence, and every Immense One I have ever met stands in front of that door and weeps, or waits, or schemes. They think it is the shape of everything. The great wall at the end of everything."
He tipped his head back and looked up at the red sky.

"I have watched them. A great many of them, through a great many eyes. Every one of them sees the door, and sees themselves, and sees nothing else. That is the trouble with being born whole. You spend your whole existence trying to stay that way."
He smiled.

"I was never whole. I was riven. Torn into pieces and scattered across more vessels than I can count. And when you are already in pieces, there is nothing a door can keep out of you. You simply go around it. You go through the walls. You eat whatever stands on the other side."
The Chorus behind him hummed.
"No door," THE Sealed One said softly, "was ever sealed for me."
He looked across the undefinition, at the Widow, at the ghost, at the blazing column of ink and time, and his gold eyes shone with something very old and very hungry.
"After all," he said,"I have access to IT."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5833: Those Who Remain!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The dead Wheel was still turning above them, whole and humming, when Poona’s voice arrived in Noah’s head.
It came bright and quick down the thread that bound her to his Tree, and it was very excited.
Moriarty had reached out to her, she told him.

The Council of Immense Ones of THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity had reached a conclusion regarding his distinction as THE Legacy’s Son. They wanted her to bring him to Lucy’s Lecture Hall. Now, if possible. Preferably sooner.
Noah opened his eyes!
Bob was watching him from his golden cloud, singularity eyes narrowed.
"Duty?" Bob asked.
"Something like that."
"Go on, then." Bob waved a tentacle at him.
"I’ll be here..."
Noah stood, brushed off his cloud, and stepped out of the dream.
Poona was waiting for him at the edge of his Domain, bouncing so hard her golden body kept leaving the grss.

"Hold on to me, Master," she said. "The Lecture Hall can’t be reached by just anyone. Only a recognized Immensity of the Legacy can find the way. Even Progeny who have lived on the mountains for Ages have never seen it."
Noah laid a hand on her small round back.
She took them through!

It felt very different from stepping through a dream. Poona’s Dream Immensity opened, warm and smelling faintly of honey, and pulled them sideways out of the Domain and into the weavings of existence itself.

Noah felt them pass between threads hidden from him until now, strands of Lucy’s old work running through the Legacy like hidden corridors behind the walls of a great house. Some of the threads were older than anything he had ever touched. Some of them hummed when Poona passed, and let her through, as a door knows its own key.
Whatever Lucy had built, it still recognized its people.
Then the threads opened, and they stepped out into light!
They stood at the center of a ring!

It was obsidian, veined with bright gold, laid flat beneath their feet like the floor of a stage. Around it ran another ring, wider, and around that another, and another, each one rising a little higher than the last, ring after ring after ring of obsidian and gold stretching out and up and away until their end lay beyond his sight. They simply kept going, climbing into a distance that had no ceiling.
An amphitheater. The largest one he had ever seen, or would likely ever see.
And on every ring, there were thrones!

Some were carved from stone and some grown from living wood. Some were made of light, or water, or bone, or things he had no name for. They stood on the tiers in a great curving sweep, and on them, or standing beside them, or drifting above them, were the Immense Ones of THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.
More than a hundred of them!
Noah’s gold eyes moved across them.

Most of them sat Established, their Profundity deep but readable, their bottoms glimpsed far below. Some sat Ancient, so deep his eyes slid off them. A handful, newly risen in the last few Ages, still burned bright and loud.

He recognized a few from the war on the Thinker’s mountain: THE Ashen Cantor with his cinders, THE Keeper of the Unbroken Vow with his chain of oaths, THE Lantern of the Last Shore with his lamp. The rest were strangers.

He spread his tentacles.

His crimson eyes met Noah’s. "Will you take it on?"

Then he reached out, and took it!

|The Legacy’s woven Immensity recognizes its bearer as its own.|
|Where the bearer walks within THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, the Legacy will answer.|

|Beyond it lies the Domain that Lucy left behind for THE Legacy’s Son.|
|No Immense One of this Legacy has entered it.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5834: I Am Sorry!
paragraphs: Noah stepped through the doorway, and the brightness closed behind him.

He braced for something grand! A vault of Immensity, perhaps. A library of lost Ages. Maybe a throne waiting at the end of a long hall, or some last weapon left by the founder of a Legacy for the one who would inherit it.
Instead, he smelled grass!
He stood at the edge of a farm!

A small one. A low wooden fence ran along a dirt path, its rails grey and soft with weather. Beyond it lay a vegetable garden in neat rows: beans climbing poles, squash sprawled under broad leaves, a line of something leafy and green gone a little wild at the end where no one had weeded it.
A field of wheat swayed gold under a pale blue sky, and past the wheat, an orchard of six apple trees, the fruit red and heavy. A single cloud drifted overhead, unhurried.
Only a mild breeze, and birdsong somewhere off in the hedges, and an absence of snow and cold and Counting so complete it felt like holding his breath.
Noah stood very still and looked at it all with his gold eyes.

Here, as far as he could feel, was simply a farm. The Gold Without Pupils went down into the soil and found soil. Into the trees and found wood and sap and apples. Into the sky and found sky, ordinary and quiet, hiding nothing at all.
So he walked!

He opened the gate, and it creaked. He walked along the dirt path between the garden rows. A hoe leaned against the fence where someone had set it down, its handle worn smooth and dark where hands had held it for a very long time. A wooden bucket sat beside a stone wel, half full of water so clear he could see the pebbles at the bottom. In the middle of the wheat stood a scarecrow with its arms out, wearing a battered straw hat and a coat patched at both elbows.
He touched the scarecrow’s sleeve as he passed. Old cloth. Real cloth. Only that.
Strange!

He had expected Lucy, THE Acharya of Immensity, founder of a Legacy where a hundred Immense Ones sat waiting for her return, to leave behind something terrible and vast. And she had left him a garden.
At the end of the path stood a hut!

It was small and plain, built of timber and stone, with a thatched roof and a crooked chimney and a single window with a flower box beneath it. Herbs grew in the flower box. Someone had planted them in careful rows.
Noah opened the door and stepped inside.

One room. A narrow bed against the wall, its blanket squared at the foot. A wooden table with two chairs. Over a hearth swept clean, a kettle hung above the cold ashes. Shelves with jars of dried beans and preserved fruit, every jar labled in a small neat hand. A pair of muddy boots by the door.
And on the table, a piece of paper!
It was gold. Thin gold, creased once, lying flat beside an empty cup. And across its face ran words in obsidian ink, small and close and slanting, written by a hand that had taken its time.
A letter!
Noah picked it up!
The moment his fingers touched it, the words began to shine!
|To the one my children chose,|

|If you are reading this, then they have named you the Legacy’s Son, and you have come through the door I left, expecting a great deal. I am sorry. There is only a farm here. I grew up on one very much like it, a long time ago, before any of the rest of it. Before Immensity, before Legacies, before any of my students learned to call me THE Acharya. I wanted whoever found this to see where I came from. I wanted them to know that I began small. Everyone does.|
|Sit down, if you like. The chair by the window is the comfortable one. This will take a while.|

|Long ago, existence turned in good order. Its cycles came and went as seasons come and go on a farm: the planting, the growing, the harvest, the long rest of winter, and then the planting again. Each cycle had its nights, and its nights were cold, but they ended. Every being that rose within a cycle could climb. There were doors above us, one after another, and a path that ran up through them, higher than any of us had ever seen. The path was hard. Most who walked it failed. But it was there, and everyone knew it was there, and that knowing was a kind of light.|

|We climbed. My friends and I. My brothers and sisters of the long road, my teachers, my students. Ages upon Ages we climbed, until we came to a place on the path that no one could pass. We called it the Narrows. A junction of existence where the path above us thinned to nothing, too fine to stand on, too high to reach. Every being who had ever reached the Narrows had stopped there, and either turned back, or remained. It was the edge of everything.|
|And beneath the Narrows, holding the whole path together, there was IT.|

|I will not tell you exactly what IT was. Partly because the words would cost you more than you can yet afford to know. And partly because I am ashamed. IT was never meant for us. IT was the thing that held the path in place, as a keystone holds an arch. IT was what let existence climb from one cycle to the next without falling apart. Nobody was meant to touch IT. Nobody was meant to use IT.|
|We used IT.|

|There were a few of us. I will not write their names, because they do not deserve to be remembered for this, and neither do I. We were the oldest, the deepest, the most certain. We had stood at the Narrows longer than anyone, and we had grown tired of standing. One of us found a way to reach beneath the path and take hold of IT. And we told each other it would only be for a moment. Just long enough to cross. Just long enough to see what lay above. We would let go on the other side, and everything would be as it was.|
|We crossed.|
|And the moment we crossed, the path broke behind us.|

|I have spent a very long time trying to describe what happened next, and I have never found the right words. IT was not made to carry anyone. When we leaned our whole weight on IT, IT split. IT sundered. IT broke apart into pieces, and the pieces were flung out across existence in every direction, far and wide and deep, into places none of us could follow. And without IT holding the path together, the path itself came apart. The Narrows collapsed. The doors above them shattered, one after another, all the way up. Everything that had held existence’s cycles in good order came loose at once.|
|That was THE First Sundering. Not a war. Not a monster. Not a curse laid on existence by some enemy. It was us. Many of us, reaching for what was not ours, and breaking everything to have it.|
|We left. We crossed over, and we went on, and the road we came by closed behind us forever.|
|And everyone else stayed.|

|My friends who had not yet reached the Narrows. My students, who had been climbing behind me their whole lives, trusting the path to be there when they arrived. My brothers and sisters who were only a few steps short. All of them stayed, because there was no longer anywhere to go. We made them what they are.We made them Those Who Remain. They did not fail. We failed them. We took the path away and left them standing on a broken stair.|
|It cannot be fixed.|

|Not by any of them, and not by you. Not even if someone gathered every piece of IT from every corner of existence and put them all back together. What broke is not only IT. What broke is the path, and the doors, and the order of existence itself. You cannot unbreak a stair by finding the stones. The shape it held is gone.|
|And existence remembers what we did to it.|

|Since the First Sundering, the cycles have turned without order. Existence is hurt, and like anything that is hurt, it is trying to heal, and its healing is not gentle. It seeks to right the wrongs done to it. Its nights will grow longer and colder and stranger than any night before. It will close what we left open. It will count what we left uncounted. It will judge anything that reaches upward, because the last ones who reached upward broke everything. I have seen the first of these nights from the other side, and I tell you plainly, worse ones are coming. The Long Night is only the beginning of its anger.|
|No doors will open. The doors were shattered so that we could leave. There is no path above. There is no sky. For those I left behind, there is no hope of going where I went.|

|You will hear prophecies. You will hear of Auguries, of keys and of those who will open the way, of signs in the snow and promises in the dark.Many of them were left behind by those of us who felt guilty.We wanted to give the ones we abandoned something to hold. Some of us whispered hopes into the cracks as we crossed. Some of us left riddles, believing that a riddle was kinder than the truth. I did it too. I left my children a chair and a cup of tea and a promise that the right key might one day open a certain door. Forgive me. It was the only kindness I knew how to leave that was not a lie, and it is very nearly one.|

|If there is anything at all to be done, it is this. The pieces of IT still lie scattered across existence. Whoever gathered them might, perhaps, do what we did once. Not repair the path. Nothing will repair the path. But cross, as we crossed, by some other way that none of us could see. Maybe. I do not know. Maybe.|

sentences.text: Noah stepped through the doorway, and the brightness closed behind him.
He braced for something grand!
A vault of Immensity, perhaps.
A library of lost Ages.
Maybe a throne waiting at the end of a long hall, or some last weapon left by the founder of a Legacy for the one who would inherit it.
Instead, he smelled grass!
He stood at the edge of a farm!
A small one.
A low wooden fence ran along a dirt path, its rails grey and soft with weather.
Beyond it lay a vegetable garden in neat rows: beans climbing poles, squash sprawled under broad leaves, a line of something leafy and green gone a little wild at the end where no one had weeded it.
A field of wheat swayed gold under a pale blue sky, and past the wheat, an orchard of six apple trees, the fruit red and heavy.
A single cloud drifted overhead, unhurried.
Only a mild breeze, and birdsong somewhere off in the hedges, and an absence of snow and cold and Counting so complete it felt like holding his breath.
Noah stood very still and looked at it all with his gold eyes.
Here, as far as he could feel, was simply a farm.
The Gold Without Pupils went down into the soil and found soil.
Into the trees and found wood and sap and apples.
Into the sky and found sky, ordinary and quiet, hiding nothing at all.
So he walked!
He opened the gate, and it creaked.
He walked along the dirt path between the garden rows.
A hoe leaned against the fence where someone had set it down, its handle worn smooth and dark where hands had held it for a very long time.
A wooden bucket sat beside a stone wel, half full of water so clear he could see the pebbles at the bottom.
In the middle of the wheat stood a scarecrow with its arms out, wearing a battered straw hat and a coat patched at both elbows.
He touched the scarecrow’s sleeve as he passed.
Old cloth.
Real cloth.
Only that.
Strange!
He had expected Lucy, THE Acharya of Immensity, founder of a Legacy where a hundred Immense Ones sat waiting for her return, to leave behind something terrible and vast.
And she had left him a garden.
At the end of the path stood a hut!
It was small and plain, built of timber and stone, with a thatched roof and a crooked chimney and a single window with a flower box beneath it.
Herbs grew in the flower box.
Someone had planted them in careful rows.
Noah opened the door and stepped inside.
One room.
A narrow bed against the wall, its blanket squared at the foot.
A wooden table with two chairs.
Over a hearth swept clean, a kettle hung above the cold ashes.
Shelves with jars of dried beans and preserved fruit, every jar labled in a small neat hand.
A pair of muddy boots by the door.
And on the table, a piece of paper!
It was gold.
Thin gold, creased once, lying flat beside an empty cup.
And across its face ran words in obsidian ink, small and close and slanting, written by a hand that had taken its time.
A letter!
Noah picked it up!
The moment his fingers touched it, the words began to shine!
|To the one my children chose,|
|If you are reading this, then they have named you the Legacy’s Son, and you have come through the door I left, expecting a great deal.
I am sorry.
There is only a farm here.
I grew up on one very much like it, a long time ago, before any of the rest of it.
Before Immensity, before Legacies, before any of my students learned to call me THE Acharya.
I wanted whoever found this to see where I came from.
I wanted them to know that I began small.
Everyone does.|
|Sit down, if you like.
The chair by the window is the comfortable one.
This will take a while.|
|Long ago, existence turned in good order.
Its cycles came and went as seasons come and go on a farm: the planting, the growing, the harvest, the long rest of winter, and then the planting again.
Each cycle had its nights, and its nights were cold, but they ended.
Every being that rose within a cycle could climb.
There were doors above us, one after another, and a path that ran up through them, higher than any of us had ever seen.
The path was hard.
Most who walked it failed.
But it was there, and everyone knew it was there, and that knowing was a kind of light.|
|We climbed.
My friends and I.
My brothers and sisters of the long road, my teachers, my students.
Ages upon Ages we climbed, until we came to a place on the path that no one could pass.
We called it the Narrows.
A junction of existence where the path above us thinned to nothing, too fine to stand on, too high to reach.
Every being who had ever reached the Narrows had stopped there, and either turned back, or remained.
It was the edge of everything.|
|And beneath the Narrows, holding the whole path together, there was IT.|
|I will not tell you exactly what IT was.
Partly because the words would cost you more than you can yet afford to know.
And partly because I am ashamed.
IT was never meant for us.
IT was the thing that held the path in place, as a keystone holds an arch.
IT was what let existence climb from one cycle to the next without falling apart.
Nobody was meant to touch IT.
Nobody was meant to use IT.|
|We used IT.|
|There were a few of us.
I will not write their names, because they do not deserve to be remembered for this, and neither do I.
We were the oldest, the deepest, the most certain.
We had stood at the Narrows longer than anyone, and we had grown tired of standing.
One of us found a way to reach beneath the path and take hold of IT.
And we told each other it would only be for a moment.
Just long enough to cross.
Just long enough to see what lay above.
We would let go on the other side, and everything would be as it was.|
|We crossed.|

IT was not made to carry anyone.
When we leaned our whole weight on IT, IT split.
IT sundered.
IT broke apart into pieces, and the pieces were flung out across existence in every direction, far and wide and deep, into places none of us could follow.
And without IT holding the path together, the path itself came apart.
The Narrows collapsed.
The doors above them shattered, one after another, all the way up.
Everything that had held existence’s cycles in good order came loose at once.|

Not a war.
Not a monster.
Not a curse laid on existence by some enemy.
It was us.
Many of us, reaching for what was not ours, and breaking everything to have it.|
|We left.
We crossed over, and we went on, and the road we came by closed behind us forever.|
|And everyone else stayed.|
|My friends who had not yet reached the Narrows.
My students, who had been climbing behind me their whole lives, trusting the path to be there when they arrived.
My brothers and sisters who were only a few steps short.
All of them stayed, because there was no longer anywhere to go.
We made them what they are.We made them Those Who Remain.
They did not fail.
We failed them.
We took the path away and left them standing on a broken stair.|
|It cannot be fixed.|

Not even if someone gathered every piece of IT from every corner of existence and put them all back together.
What broke is not only IT.
What broke is the path, and the doors, and the order of existence itself.
You cannot unbreak a stair by finding the stones.
The shape it held is gone.|

The Long Night is only the beginning of its anger.|

Forgive me.

Maybe.|

paragraphs: Noah set the letter down on the table, beside the empty cup, exactly where he had found it.
Then he went outside.

The breeze was still blowing. The wheat still swayed. Somewhere in the hedges, the same bird was still singing, as though beings breaking the path above existence and leaving countless to freeze were a story about somewhere else. This little farm had kept on being a farm through all of it.
He stood on the doorstep for a while and looked at the garden.

The row at the end had gone wild. Weeds had crept in among the greens, tall and tangled, as weeds always do when a garden is left alone. The beans had climbed past the tops of their poles and were waving loose in the air. A few apples had fallen in the orchard and lay in the grass, going soft.
Noah walked down the path to the fence, picked up the old hoe leaning against it, and turned it over in his hands.
Smooth wood. Dark where hands had held it. Heavier than it looked.
He smiled a little.

It was a silly thing to want, for a being like him. He had evolved. He had eaten a dead Immense One and an Ergosphere full of Roots and two suns made of civilizations. And for all of that, one of the grandest dreams he had ever carried was this: a farm. A small one. Somewhere quiet, when everything was over and done, with a garden to tend and a family to feed and nothing more urgent anywhere than whether the beans needed tying.
He rolled up imaginary sleeves, and went to work!

He started with the weeds, kneeling in the wild row and pulling them one by one, roots and all, shaking the dirt off and tossing them in a pile at the end of the path. The soil was cool and dark and smelled of rian. Next, he tied the beans back to their poles with lengths of twine he found hanging on a nail by the hut door.

He gathered the fallen apples into the wooden bukcet and set them by the well. Last, he drew water and carried it down the rows and poured it at the roots of every plant, slowly, watching the soil drink.
His stellar dark gold hands got dirty.
Then he took the hoe to the last row.

It was hard ground, packed down from Ages without a turning, and he worked it. Lift, drop, pull. Lift, drop, pull. The blade bit into the earth and turned it over, dark and crumbling, and the smell of it rose up around him.
It was cathartic.
On the seventh stroke, the blade caught on something.
Paper!
A little scrap of it, crumpled into a ball, half buried in the soil where the hoe had turned it up. Gold, like the letter. Old, and creased, and very small.
Noah crouched and picked it up.
It was heavy. Far too heavy for a scrap of paper. His hand dipped under the weight of it, as though he had picked up a stone pretending to be a leaf. He stared at it for a moment.
Then he smoothed it open on his palm!
BOOM!

Something sat in the creases of the paper. A shard. Tiny, no larger than a grain of sand, obsidian and gold, catching the mild farm light and throwing it back as a deep, impossible gleam. And the moment the paper opened and the shard touched open air, its weight came down.
All of it!

Noah’s arm dropped. His knees drove into the soft dirt of the garden row. The grain of obsidian and gold sat on his open palm and pressed down on him with a heaviness beyond anything in his life. Heavier than the stone he had carried on his back in the obsidian sands. Heavier than the Warden’s gaze. Heavier than the Hound’s closing hand, or the Fiend’s finger, or any Judgment existence had ever dropped on him. It was so heavy that the farm itself seemed to lean toward it, the wheat bowing, the apple trees creaking, the single cloud overhead drifting slowly down.
On the inside of the paper, in small slanting obsidian ink, there were words.

|It seems you are a decent being. You did not destroy everything in rage, and you even began taking care of my farm. So here is a little fragment I managed to hold, and keep down here. I doubt it will help much, or change much. But it is something.|
BOOM!
The prompts came, and they were short.
|Obtained: an Infinitesimally Small Shard of IT.|
|Details: ???|
|Details: ???|
|Details: ???|
Noah stared at the shard in his palm.
A piece of IT!

A grain of the thing that had once held the whole path of existence together, before beings leaned their weight on it and broke it apart. Lucy had kept this. Hidden it in the dirt of her own garden, under her own scarecrow, where only someone willing to kneel in the soil and pull weeds would ever find it.
His existence pulsed!

It pulsed hard, once, all the way through, as though every part of him had just heard its own name called. The Tree in his chest flared. And his eyes, his pure gold pupil-less eyes, burned. Bright. Brighter!
Blazing with something between hunger and defiance, both at once, a gold fire so fierce it lit the garden row around him.
He could barely hold the shard up. His arm shook under it. His fingers trembled.
And something in him said: eat it.
Fucking it eat bro!
It skipped every step of thought. His existence wanted it, completely and instinctively, as a starving thing wants bread. So he lifted his trembling hand to his mouth.
And brought his jaws down.
It went into him like a mountain falling into a well.

The weight that had driven him to his knees was suddenly inside him, and his whole existence buckled around it. He felt it drop through him, past his tongue, past his throat, down into the heart of everything he was, and land at the base of his Tree like an anvil dropped from the sky.
BOOM!
His body shook!

His skin stretched. All over, at once, the night-dark surface of him bulged outward in a hundred places, as though spears were trying to push their way out of him from the inside. His constellations blazed and scattered. His horns of radiance flickered wildly.

The halo of time behind his shoulders spun so fast it shrieked. He could feel cracks running through his existence, fine and many, the whole of him straining to hold something far beyond what it had been built to hold.
He sat down!

Right there in the garden, in the dirt between the bean rows, cross-legged, hands on his knees. He closed his gold eyes and turned everything he had inward. His Dream. The Tree where his Root had been. The Human and the Dreamer and the Sovereign in him, all at once.
Then the Dreaming Human Origin went to work on what he had swallowed.

Instead of fighting it, he dreamed around it. He wrapped it in Dream, layer upon layer, and began, slowly, to break it down, as he had broken down the corpse of an Immense One and an Ergosphere full of Roots.
But this was different. This held. This was the oldest, densest, most fundamental thing he had ever touched, and his Dream could only wear at it, grain by grain, as a river wears at a mountain.
So he let time pass.
He let a great deal of it pass!
And as it passed, he saw himself.
He saw himself young. A boy, thin and quick, holding a hoe too big for him in the school garden and laughing at something just out of sight.

He saw himself as he was when everything first broke, frightened and furious, throwing fire with shaking hands. He saw himself crushed under a stone in the obsidian sands. Kneeling over a corpse on a frozen plain. Standing on a cloud while a door slammed in a young woman’s face.
He saw himself now, sitting in the dirt.
And he saw himself old.

Old, as he had always refused to imagine being. Grey at the temples. Lined at the eyes. Sitting on a porch very much like the one behind him, watching a garden grow, with children’s voices somewhere out in the wheat, and a cup of tea going cold in his hand. Content!

And then he saw more. Lives still unlived, that he might yet live. A thousand Noahs, a million, branching away in every direction through the long dream, each one living out a whole existence in the space of a breath.

One who ruled. One who wandered. One who farmed. One who died young and one who lived forever. He lived them all. Every year of them. Every season. It felt like a very long time, and also no time at all, as a whole life feels at the end of it.
All of it, every life and every year, went into the shard, and wore at it, and wore at it.
And the shard, very slowly, gave.
His body settled!

The spears beneath his skin sank back. The cracks in his existence sealed, one after another, and where each one closed, something new and dense and gold remained behind. His constellations drifted back into place under his skin. The halo behind his shoulders slowed, and steadied, and when it settled, there were two rings turning there, one inside the other.
Noah opened his eyes!
In the gold of them, very faint, a fleck of obsidian now drifted.
|Devoured: an Infinitesimally Small Shard of IT.|
|What you devoured cannot be fully understood. Your existence has taken from it only what it can hold.|
|Your Tree has drunk deeply.|
|Sap risen: 100%. Your Tree has grown its First Bough.|
|A great limb spreads from your trunk, and your existence spreads with it.|
|Second Ring lit. Ring by ring, your trunk will burn brighter, until one day it blazes from root to crown.|
|Sap risen toward the Second Bough: 90%.|
|Attributes, measured anew.|
|VERITAS: Order I.8 to Order II.6.|
|PROVENANCE: Order I.9 to Order II.7.|
|PONDUS: Order I.8 to Order II.3.|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: Order I.5 to Order II.0.|
|POTENTIA: Infinite.|
|Every attribute has entered the second Order. Your Dream now reaches across the whole domain of a Legacy.|
|Predation: from the Shard of IT, your Tree has drawn a capability.|
|Formed: THE Keystone Dream.|

|Every structure has a stone that holds it: a being, a power, a Domain, a seal, a curse, a Legacy. You see that stone. You may dream it loose, and let all it held come apart. Or you may dream it held, and let nothing break it.|
|Your reach follows your Order. Keystones set deeper than your Profundity lie below your sight.|
|IT was a keystone once. You now carry a grain of it, and you will never look at anything the same way again.|
|Auto-Fusion: THE Keystone Dream + THE First Unsealing: THE Door of Immensity.|

|THE First Unsealing has deepened. It is now THE Unsealing of Doors. Every door has a keystone. What is closed against those you lift, you may find the stone of, and open; what is sealed against yourself, you may find the stone of, and seek a way through.|
|Kin: your Tree has risen. Those bound to it rise with it.|
|Ling, Poona, and Bob have deepened. The cocoons of your Kin brighten.|
|Your Gold Without Pupils has been refined. You may now perceive the weavings of IT.|
|Sensed, faintly: Shards of IT, resonating with the one you devoured.|
|Several lie within THE Undersnow.|
|Others are stretched across existence, beyond your present reach. Some may rest in the hands of Legacies.|
|This Domain lies beyond the sight of existence. No Judgment reaches here.|
|For now.|
Noah sat in the dirt between the bean rows for a long time after the prompts stopped.

He could feel them. The Shards! Faint, very faint, like the warmth of distant fires felt through a closed door. Several of them below, deep in THE Undersnow, down past the Basal Floor, past the rift, somewhere in the frozen dark of the Evergrave and beyond. Others farther. Much farther. Scattered across existence, some of them humming in places beyond his sight, some of them, he was almost sure, held tight in the grip of someone very old.

Lucy’s letter said it was beyond fixing. Lucy’s letter said there was no path, and no sky, and no hope for Those Who Remain. Lucy had been there. Lucy knew more than anyone alive about what had broken, and how badly.
Noah looked down at his dirty hands.
"Nothing is impossible," he said quietly, to himself, to the farm, to the scarecrow in the wheat.
The breeze moved through the beans.
"Whether the path is fully closed or not," Noah said, "I will decide that. Not her. Not existence. Me."
He picked up the hoe again, and stood, and looked out over the half-tended garden and the gold wheat and the six apple trees, and felt the faint warmth of the Shards far below, calling.
"IT," he said, "is a good place to start."

The Human and the Dreamer and the Sovereign in him, all at once.
Then the Dreaming Human Origin went to work on what he had swallowed.
Instead of fighting it, he dreamed around it.
He wrapped it in Dream, layer upon layer, and began, slowly, to break it down, as he had broken down the corpse of an Immense One and an Ergosphere full of Roots.
But this was different.
This held.
This was the oldest, densest, most fundamental thing he had ever touched, and his Dream could only wear at it, grain by grain, as a river wears at a mountain.
So he let time pass.
He let a great deal of it pass!

He saw himself young.

chapters.title: Chapter 5836: Order II
paragraphs: Noah set the hoe back against the fence where he had found it.
He looked at the garden one last time. Weeds lay piled at the end of the path, the beans stood tied to their poles, and the apples sat in the bucket by the well. It was unfinished. A farm always was.
He walked back to the doorway at the edge of the fields and stopped.

A hundred Immense Ones were waiting on the other side of it. He could feel their attention pressing faintly against the door like a crowd against a window. The moment he stepped through, they would want answers.
He wanted a few of his own first.
So he lifted THE Orb of Immensity and asked it, plainly, for somewhere quiet.
The Orb answered!

Lucy’s script turned inside it in slow gold rings, and the tiny door at its heart swung to face a different way. When Noah stepped through the brightness, he stood on the shoulder of a lonley mountain at the far edge of the Legacy, snow up to his knees, wind howling across bare rock. An old shrine sat half buried in the drifts. Below it, a frozen pond lay cracked straight across from the war.
The Legacy had heard its Son, and sent him where nobody would be watching!
Noah sat down in the snow, crossed his legs, and closed his gold eyes.
Then he let his Dream go as he wanted to test out his existence...at Order II.
It went out of him like breath on a cold morning, and it kept going.

Over the shrine. Over the cracked pond. Down the mountain’s side and across the valley below, over the purple-gold rivers running dark between the peaks, up the next mountain and the next. His Dream spread across the snow like a tide coming in over a beach, soft and wide and quiet, and everything it touched became something he could feel.

He felt the Keepers’ Roads winding between the mountains, every stone of them. He felt the Existential Conduits rising out of the rivers, every thread of light in their columns. Then came the thousand Elsedimension Mountains, one after another after another, and then, as his Dream sank into them, he felt what lay inside.
Dimensions!

Every mountain held them. Some held one, vast and quiet. Some held dozens, stacked inside the stone like rooms in a great house. And inside those Dimensions, Observable Existences, turning slowly in their own skies, each one full of light and motion and life.
Domains, Wheels, Frequencies, Cosmos, Galaxies, Seas. Forests under strange suns. Peoples living out their lives inside the mountains of a Legacy they would only ever know from within.
His Dream passed through all of it, and all of it began, very faintly, to dream.
He felt the lives in them, all at once rather than one at a time. Countless points of light scattered through the Legacy like stars through a night sky, each one a life, each one going about its day.

A child running down a street in a city inside a mountain; a farmer in a field under a sky with three moons; a Progeny meditating on a monastary terrace, a Root humming in her chest; a Keeper sweeping snow off the steps of a throne.
He felt the Immense Ones!

They burned among the lesser lights like suns. These were apart from the hundred in Lucy’s Lecture Hall; that place sat apart from everything else, a bright sealed knot in the weavings of the Legacy, too tightly woven for his Dream to enter. These were the others.

The Immense who kept to their own mountains. Dozens of them, scattered across the Legacy, each one deep, each one different. One sat alone on a peak of red stone, unmoving, its Profundity going down past his sight.
Another drifted through a Dimension of endless water, singing to itself. A third walked the Keepers’ Roads in the shape of an old woman with a basket, and the snow fell differently around her.
Every one of them went on, unaware of him!

His Dream lay over the whole Legacy, touching every one of them, and every head stayed exactly where it was. The old woman with the basket walked on, the singer in the water kept singing, and the Immense One on the red peak sat as still as it had sat for Ages.
His dreaming slid past their senses entirely!
Noah sat very still in the snow on his lonely mountain, and let that settle.
He went deeper!
Beneath the mountains, beneath the purple-gold rivers, beneath the snow-buried floor of the whole Legacy, his Dream found something unexpected.
Domains!

Existential Immense Domains, sunk into the foundations of the Legacy like vaults beneath a palace. Dozens of them. Sealed, silent, dark. His Dream slipped into the first one, and found it full of stone.
Statues!
They stood in rows in the dark, vast and still. Statues of Immense Ones, every one of them different. One the shape of a great Sphinx with antlers like the branches of a winter forest.

Another, a woman made of interlocking rings. A tower with eyes. A beast so large its head was lost in the dark above. Some as small as a man. Some larger than the Domain that held them, somehow, their edges trailing away into a scale his Dream could barely hold.
And every one of them was sleeping!
He could feel it. Under the stone, something breathed. Slowly. Once an Age, perhaps. A Profundity in every statue, deep and quiet and enormous, curled up in the dark like a seed in winter ground.

He moved to the next Domain. Statues. The next. Statues. Dozens of Domains, hundreds of statues, all of them Immense, all of them asleep, all of them hidden beneath a Legacy whose living Immense Ones walked over their heads every day and kept every word about them to themselves.
|Sensed: Existential Immense Domains beneath THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.|
|Within them: Immense Ones, in the form of statues, sleeping.|
|Their nature: ???|
Noah’s breath went out of him, slowly.

Who were they? Lucy’s students, who had remained and found it too much to bear? Companions of the leavers, put to sleep before the crossing? Something the Legacy had chosen to forget? Did Moriarty know? Did the Thinker?
The answers lay beyond him, for now. He held the questions, and kept going.
There was more to learn, and he learned it fast.

Each of those countless lights scattered across the Legacy, every Progeny, every Provenance Lifeform, every being with a Root humming in its chest, lay inside his Dream. He could feel their Roots. He could feel the edges of them.
And he understood, with a cold and perfect clarity, what that meant.

If he wished it, he could end them. From here. A Root-holder on a mountain at the other end of the Legacy, meditating peacefully on a terrace, would simply stop. He could dream their end as he had dreamed the Guards’ ends on the Basal Floor, and its source would stay hidden from them forever. Or he could open his mouth on this lonely mountain, and their Roots would come to him across the whole Legacy and go down into his Tree.

He could be anywhere! He reached out to the monastery terrace, and his Dream gathered there, and for a moment he was standing beside the meditating Progeny, close enough to see the snow on her eyelashes. She kept her eyes closed.
He reached to the water Dimension and stood beside the singing Immense One, close enough to hear the words of its song. It sang on.
He could stand beside a Newly Risen Immense One in its own Domain, and strike, and it would feel only the blow, after it had already landed.
All of it was his to do. Across the whole breadth of a Legacy!
This was his power! His Infinite Dream!
Noah opened his eyes.
The snow fell on his lonely mountain. Far below, the cracked pond lay quiet.

He thought, calmly, that this was what it was to be a dreamer at Order II. To lie over a whole Legacy like the night lies over a sleeping town, seeing every window, every lamp, every life, and to be seen by none of them. Every one of those lights was a choice he could make. End it. Keep it. Eat it. Leave it alone. Watching them from here, he could see every way each of them might go, every branch, every future, all of it laid out like the lines on an open palm.
It would have been very easy to stop seeing them as people.
He refused to let himself. He looked at the child running down the street inside the mountain, and made himself see a child. And on the terrace, the Progeny: he saw the snow on her eyelashes.
Then he let his Dream draw back, slowly, from all of them.
Power like this was a grand thing. He would carry it as he carried everything else, and use it when he chose.
At the very edge of his withdrawing Dream, in the bright sealed knot of the Lecture Hall, something clicked.
A single bead, sliding along a string.
Noah went still!
He waited. Silence followed: one click, faint as a pin dropped in snow, and then stillness.
Perhaps it was nothing.
He doubted it.
He tested the rest quickly.

THE Keystone Dream first. He looked at the old shrine’s ward, a faint skin of protection laid down over its stones by some Progeny long ago, and the ward lit in his sight like a web of frost, every strand leading inward to a single rune cut into the lintel. He dreamed it loose, and the ward came apart in silence, falling away like frost melting off glass. Then he dreamed it held, and the ward knit itself back together, good as new.
Then he tried the Legacy itself, out of pure curiosity.

He followed Lucy’s weavings inward, every river and Conduit and mountain bound together in threads so old they had hardened into something like stone. He followed them down toward the place where they all had to meet.
And lost them!

They went down past his sight, into a Profundity his gold eyes were unable to follow. Lucy’s keystone lay below him. Far below. So did his own; when he turned THE Keystone Dream inward, it found only the endless trunk of his Tree going down past anything he could see.

Last, the edge of his reach. He pushed his Dream out past the farthest mountain of the Legacy, toward the cracked sky at its border, and tried to dream a single snowflake beyond the border into a Dimension.

The dream thinned as it went, stretching like honey pulled too far, until at the Legacy’s edge it simply stopped. Inside the border, a Dimension bloomed in the air, blue-gold, and drifted down into the drifts as asnowflake was made into a Dimension.Beyond it, the snowflake stayed a snowflake.
Order II: a Legacy’s whole breadth, everything inside it!
|Order II, measured.|
|Your Dream covers the whole domain of a Legacy. Within it, you perceive every Dimension, every Observable Existence, every Root, and every Immensity, and none perceive your dreaming.|
|Within it, you may stand anywhere as though dreaming there, and impose your power wherever you wish.|
|Within it, those who hold only Roots are yours to end, or to devour.|
|Within it, a Newly Risen Immensity will sense you only when your blow has landed.|
|Established and Ancient Immensities will sense you when you act near or upon them.|
|A notice, on your progress.|
|The Sap thickens as it nears a Bough.|
|You rose swiftly, carried by a Shard of IT. That was a gift, and gifts of that kind are rare. From here, your Tree grows at its true pace.|

|The final stretch toward the Second Bough will demand far more than the first. Ordinary loot will barely stir the Sap. Only grand loot will move it: the corpses of the Immense, the Ergospheres of Roots, and more.|
|Sap risen toward the Second Bough: 90%.|
Noah read it twice, and almost laughed out loud!
Ten percent. And those ten percent would cost him more than the ninety before them.
Okay!
But he learned a great deal.

A Dream that covered a whole Legacy, unseen. Every Root inside it his to end or eat. Newly Risen Immense, open to him before they knew he was there. THE Keystone Dream, proven. A secret beneath the Legacy that its own Immense Ones had kept silent about.
He was stronger than he had ever been. And somewhere under the Legacy, a few hundred Immense Ones were sleeping in stone.
He turned his face toward the floor of everything.

Beneath the Legacy, beneath the snow, beneath the frozen dark of the Basal Floor, he could feel them now that he was quiet: several warmths, faint and far down, calling to the grain of IT in him like coals answering a spark.
Shards below. Unclaimed!
When he went down into THE Evergrave, he would let his Dream go there too to learn.
Noah lifted the Orb. The tiny door at its heart turned back toward the Lecture Hall, and opened.

He stepped through, and came out at the bottom of a bowl of obsidian and gold, where more than a hundred Immense Ones were still sitting exactly where he had left them, leaning forward on their thrones.
And on the innermost ring, the Thinker’s beads clicked once, slowly, as he passed.

Like this...an entire Legacy was slowly mobilized!

Noah looked at it with THE Keystone Dream.

That one!

CRACK!

The gate stood open!
He walked through. Behind him, he dreamed the bone back into its place, and the frost closed over the ribs again.

Beneath it lay the Evergrave.

A Dimension, or the bones of one. Light years of distance of Streets of black ice ran out from the gate in straight lines wider than rivers, so smooth they held the dead sun’s reflection. Towers and halls and houses lined them, built for bodies other than human, dead so long their shapes had stopped making sense. A few windows glowed a faint blue. Shapes moved slowly behind some of them, as if every step cost them something.
And over all of it, the anger!

It came down on him the moment he passed the gate. Heavy, and constant, and old. It settled on the back of his neck like a hand and stayed there. The anger soaked the ice under his feet and the dead sun overhead and every stone of every frozen house. It had been here so long that it had stopped being a feeling and become the weather.
And it looked at him. The only living thing in its home.
|You have entered the place where existence keeps its anger.|
|It will press on you.|
|It will remember you.|
Noah rolled his shoulders under the weight, and smiled.
Across the street, a door creaked open.

A dead thing stood in it, weaker than anything with a Root.Tall, thin, wrapped in rags stiff with frost, its face a grey shape with dark hollows where its eyes had been. It had come to the door slowly, drawn by something it had no name for.
Then it felt him!

It flinched back so hard it hit the doorframe. Its hands came up in front of its face as if he were a fire roaring in its doorway. A sound came out of it, thin and cracked, a word in some language older than any he knew. Noah understood it anyway.
Warm.
It said the word as a man alone in the dark might say knife.
Then it was gone, the door slamming, its footsteps scraping away inside. Up and down the street, the blue windows went dark one after another.
Noah watched them go out.
He had walked into many places in his life. This was the first where warmth was the thing people hid from.
Night Lifeforms here were interesting!
None antagonized him so far, so he didn’t rush out to be a genocidal maniac just yet.
He sat down on the black ice, crossed his legs, closed his gold eyes, and let his Dream go.

It went out over the Evergrave soft and wide and silent, as it had gone over the Legacy, rolling down the streets and in through the dark windows and out across the frozen land beyond. The Evergrave was bigger than any Legacy. His Dream covered only part of it before it thinned and stopped. Maybe a tenth.
He felt the dead. Thousands upon thosuands of them, in the city light years vast, alone, kept awake in the cold. Every one of them went on, unaware of him passing.

He felt them gathered in families. Clans and Provenance Lineages. Each one held a stretch of the city or the frozen land beyond it, with high walls of ice, banners of stitched skin, and a strong one at the center. The clan heads burned among the lesser Night Lifeforms like cold suns, deep and dangerous, every one of them Immense.Newly Risen, and even Established!
He felt the clans at work!

On a long street near the city’s edge, a column of weak dead stood chained together, and tall figures in grey robes walked the line with glass needles. Wherever a needle went in, something pale and gold drifted out of the dead and up into glass jars. The dead in that line went dimmer every time. Warm memories, he understood: a fire, a hand, a summer day. They were draining the last warmth out of the weakest dead and keeping it in jars.

Beyond the city, he felt fields where the dimmest of all had been planted upright in the ice, row on row, and set alight. They burned slowly, with a pale fire that gave no heat, and their light was carried away in lanterns to light the clans’ halls.
He felt four things that were bigger than the Provenance Lineages. Much bigger!

A king of frost on a throne of bone at the city’s heart, thin as a starved man, wearing a crown made of finger-bones; a cathedral shaped like a woman, with a choir inside her singing something that sounded like an apology; a giant drowned and frozen under a sea of black ice, screaming without a sound; and far off, at the very edge of his reach, something armored and old and utterly still, sitting before a gate.
Established, all four. Their Profundity went down past anything he could see. Four lords over all the Night Provenance Lineages!
And past the armored thing, past the gate, at the very center of the Evergrave, beyond the reach of his Dream, something pulsed against the grain of IT in his chest so hard it ached.
A Shard!
Noah drew his Dream back slowly, and opened his eyes.
A city of the dead, cold and awake. Clans of Immense dead, feeding on the weak. Four lords above the clans. And at the center of it all, behind every one of them, a single Shard of IT.
One Shard. Four Established Immense Ones. A great many lifeforms in the way. And his Sap needed feeding anyway.
He found he was looking forward to it!
Noah stood and brushed the frost off his knees.
Far down the street, at the edge of what he could see, something howled. Long and high and hungry, the sound of a hunting horn blown through a throat. Another howl answered it. Then another.
A dozen shapes came over the rooftops in a running pack, low and fast, their eyes cold points of blue. At their head ran something taller.
It was sniffing!
And then it turned, all at once, and looked straight down the long black street at the only warm thing in the Evergrave.
Towards him, and the glorious weavings of an Infinite Dream beginning to spill out of him!
